Armand d'Armailhac of [Château d'Armailhac](/wiki/Ch%C3%A2teau_d%27Armailhac "Château d'Armailhac") *(bottle picture)* and Baron Hector de Brane of Château Mouton were important figures in the establishment of Cabernet Sauvignon in Bordeaux.

The [Bordeaux wine region](/wiki/Bordeaux_wine_region "Bordeaux wine region") is intimately connected with Cabernet Sauvignon, even though wine is rarely made without the blended component of other grape varieties. It is the likely place of origin of the vine, and producers across the globe have invested heavily in trying to reproduce the structure and complexity of Bordeaux wines. While the "Bordeaux blend" of Cabernet Sauvignon, Cabernet Franc and Merlot created the earliest examples of acclaimed Cabernet Sauvignon wine, Cabernet Sauvignon was first blended in Bordeaux with [Syrah](/wiki/Syrah "Syrah") (from the Northern Rhone), a pairing that is widely seen in Australia and some *vin de pays* wines from the [Languedoc](/wiki/Languedoc_(wine) "Languedoc (wine)").

The decision to first start blending Cabernet Sauvignon was partly derived from financial necessity. The sometimes temperamental and unpredictable climate of Bordeaux during the "[Little Ice Age](/wiki/Little_Ice_Age "Little Ice Age")" did not guarantee a successful harvest every year; producers had to insure themselves against the risk of losing an entire vintage by planting a variety of grapes. Over time it was discovered that the unique characteristics of each grape variety could complement each other and enhance the quality of the wine. fanoutqa_006226.t: Supreme Court of the United States :: Process :: Decision :: chunk_0031
fanoutqa_006226.x:
Supreme Court of the United States :: Process :: Decision :: chunk_0031
At the conclusion of oral argument, the case is submitted for decision. Cases are decided by majority vote of the justices. After the oral argument is concluded, usually in the same week as the case was submitted, the justices retire to another conference at which the preliminary votes are tallied and the court sees which side has prevailed. One of the justices in the majority is then assigned to write the court's opinion, also known as the "majority opinion", an assignment made by the most senior justice in the majority, with the chief justice always being considered the most senior. Drafts of the court's opinion circulate among the justices until the court is prepared to announce the judgment in a particular case.[[220]](#cite_note-220)

Justices are free to change their votes on a case up until the decision is finalized and published. In any given case, a justice is free to choose whether or not to author an opinion or else simply join the majority or another justice's opinion. There are several primary types of opinions:

* **Opinion of the court**: this is the binding decision of the Supreme Court. An opinion that more than half of the justices join (usually at least five justices, since there are nine justices in total; but in cases where some justices do not participate it could be fewer) is known as "majority opinion" and creates binding precedent in American law. Whereas an opinion that fewer than half of the justices join is known as a "plurality opinion" and is only partially binding precedent.
* **Concurring**: a justice agrees with and joins the majority opinion but authors a separate concurrence to give additional explanations, rationales, or commentary. Concurrences do not create binding precedent.
* **Concurring in the judgment**: a justice agrees with the outcome the court reached but disagrees with its reasons for doing so. A justice in this situation does not join the majority

High country overnight trips require gear suitable for -35 °F or below.[[38]](#cite_note-Weather-38)

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/52/Wild_Rose_Beautiful%2C_from_the_Plains_to_the_Subalpine._Rocky_Mountain_National_Park.jpg/250px-Wild_Rose_Beautiful%2C_from_the_Plains_to_the_Subalpine._Rocky_Mountain_National_Park.jpg)](/wiki/File:Wild_Rose_Beautiful,_from_the_Plains_to_the_Subalpine._Rocky_Mountain_National_Park.jpg)

Wild roses (*[Rosa acicularis](/wiki/Rosa_acicularis "Rosa acicularis")*) bloom from montane to subalpine regions

The subalpine region does not begin to experience spring-like conditions until June. Wildflowers bloom from late June to early August.[[38]](#cite_note-Weather-38)

Below 9,400 feet (2,865 m), temperatures are often moderate, although nighttime temperatures are cool, as is typical of mountain weather.[[38]](#cite_note-Weather-38) Spring comes to the montane area by early May, when wildflowers begin to bloom. Spring weather is subject to unpredictable changes in temperature and precipitation, with potential for snow along trails through May.[[38]](#cite_note-Weather-38) In July and August, temperatures are generally in the 70s or 80s °[F](/wiki/Fahrenheit "Fahrenheit") during the day, and as low as the 40s °F at night.[[38]](#cite_note-Weather-38) Lower elevations receive rain as most of their summer precipitation.[[37]](#cite_note-LCCVP_primer_p._1-37)

[Philip Morris Companies](/wiki/Philip_Morris_Companies "Philip Morris Companies") acquired General Foods in 1985 and Kraft Inc. in 1988, eventually merging them as [Kraft Foods Inc.](/wiki/Kraft_Foods_Inc. "Kraft Foods Inc.") before the cereal unit was sold to Ralcorp in 2007.

In 2011, [Ralcorp](/wiki/Ralcorp "Ralcorp") announced plans to spin off Post Foods into a separate company. About a quarter of Ralcorp's sales in 2010 were generated by its Post Foods unit.[[14]](#cite_note-14) The spinoff was completed with an [IPO](/wiki/Initial_public_offering "Initial public offering") for Post Holdings, Inc. on February 7, 2012.[[15]](#cite_note-15)

In 2014, the company acquired Michael Foods, headquartered in [Minnetonka, Minnesota](/wiki/Minnetonka,_Minnesota "Minnetonka, Minnesota"), for $2.45 billion.[[16]](#cite_note-16)[[17]](#cite_note-17)

The following year, Post Foods purchased [MOM Brands](/wiki/MOM_Brands "MOM Brands") (formerly Malt-O-Meal Co.) creating the third largest breakfast cereal company in the US. At this point, Post Foods rebranded as Post Consumer Brands, and is headquartered in [Lakeville, Minnesota](/wiki/Lakeville,_Minnesota "Lakeville, Minnesota").

In July 2017, [Post Holdings](/wiki/Post_Holdings "Post Holdings") bought [Weetabix Limited](/wiki/Weetabix_Limited "Weetabix Limited") (including US subsidiary Barbara's) for £1.4 billion.[[18]](#cite_note-18) In 2019, the company began combining some of its MOM Brands and Weetabix cereal brands under the [Three Sisters Cereal](/wiki/Three_Sisters_Cereal "Three Sisters Cereal") name.

fanoutqa_024914.x: Hippeastrum :: Cultivation :: Dormancy :: chunk_0015 *Hippeastrum* bulbs can be induced to rebloom yearly by mimicking the conditions in its natural environment (cool dry winters). When foliage starts to yellow, dormancy can be induced by withholding water and placing the plant in a cool 4–13 °C (39–55 °F) dark place for six to ten weeks or until buds start to show. Even when plants are thriving outdoors in temperate climates, dormancy can be induced by withholding water and fertilizer in the northern hemisphere autumn, and bringing indoors to a cool environment prior to the first frost. Leaves will usually wither during this period and a flower stem begin to emerge after eight to ten weeks. Bulbs can then be brought back into light, inspected for pests or rot, and repotted in fresh soil after cutting foliage to about 10 cm above the bulb. Subsequent care is as for new bulbs, as described above. Best results are obtained by transplanting every three to four years.[[52]](#cite_note-usna-54)[[73]](#cite_note-rhs-75)[[75]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHessayon1995-77)[[95]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEOckenga2002[[Category:Wikipedia_articles_needing_page_number_citations_from_June_2020]][[[Wikipedia:Citing_sources|page needed]]]-97) The [cultivar](/wiki/Cultivar "Cultivar") 'Clown' (Double Galaxy Group)[[96]](#cite_note-98) (white with red stripes) has received the [Royal Horticultural Society](/wiki/Royal_Horticultural_Society "Royal Horticultural Society")'s [Award of Garden Merit](/wiki/Award_of_Garden_Merit "Award of Garden Merit"). * [!['Lemon Sorbet'](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/ca/Hippeastrum_Lemon_Sorbet.1c.UME.jpg/250px-Hippeastrum_Lemon_Sorbet.1c.UME.jpg)](/wiki/File:Hippeastrum_Lemon_Sorbet.1c.UME.jpg "'Lemon Sorbet'") 'Le

*The Avengers* grossed $623.4 million in the United States and Canada, and $895.5 million in other territories, for a worldwide total of $1.519 billion,[[4]](#cite_note-BOM-5) making it the [third-highest-grossing film of all time](/wiki/List_of_highest-grossing_films "List of highest-grossing films"),[[184]](#cite_note-third_highest_news-187) the [highest-grossing film of 2012](/wiki/2012_in_film "2012 in film"), the highest-grossing comic book adaptation, the highest-grossing superhero film, and the highest-grossing film ever released by Walt Disney Studios, at the time of its release.[[185]](#cite_note-highest-Disney-188) The film's worldwide opening of $392.5 million ranked as the fourth-largest.[[186]](#cite_note-world-open-189) *The Avengers* also became the fifth film distributed by [Disney](/wiki/Walt_Disney_Studios_Motion_Pictures "Walt Disney Studios Motion Pictures") and the twelfth film overall to earn more than $1 billion. It reached this milestone in 19 days, matching the record previously set by *[Avatar](/wiki/Avatar_(2009_film) "Avatar (2009 film)")* (2009) and *[Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows – Part 2](/wiki/Harry_Potter_and_the_Deathly_Hallows_%E2%80%93_Part_2 "Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows – Part 2")* (2011).[[187]](#cite_note-BOM-1billion-190)[[188]](#cite_note-HollywoodReporter16-191)[[189]](#cite_note-Time-1billion-192) Its grosses exceeded its estimated $220 million production cost 12 days after its release.[[190]](#cite_note-BoxOffice2-193) It was the first Marvel production to generate $1 billion in ticket sales.[[191]](#cite_note-TicketSales-194)

On February 9, in his first game back with the Heat, Wade was garnered a standing ovation and recorded three points, two rebounds, two assists, and two blocks off the bench in a 91–85 victory over the [Milwaukee Bucks](/wiki/Milwaukee_Bucks "Milwaukee Bucks").[[121]](#cite_note-121) On February 27, he scored a season-high 27 points and made the game-winning shot as the Heat rallied to beat the [Philadelphia 76ers](/wiki/Philadelphia_76ers "Philadelphia 76ers") 102–101.[[122]](#cite_note-122) On April 3, in a 101–98 victory over the [Atlanta Hawks](/wiki/Atlanta_Hawks "Atlanta Hawks"), Wade reached 5,000 assists in a Heat uniform, becoming the ninth player to score 20,000 points and collect 5,000 assists with one team, joining [Karl Malone](/wiki/Karl_Malone "Karl Malone"), Bryant, Jordan, James, [Larry Bird](/wiki/Larry_Bird "Larry Bird"), [John Havlicek](/wiki/John_Havlicek "John Havlicek"), [Oscar Robertson](/wiki/Oscar_Robertson "Oscar Robertson") and [Jerry West](/wiki/Jerry_West "Jerry West").[[123]](#cite_note-123) On April 16, Wade scored 28 points to end the 76ers' 17-game winning streak and lead the Heat to a 113–103 Game 2 win over Philadelphia and even the first-round playoff series. Further information: [List of California wildfires](/wiki/List_of_California_wildfires "List of California wildfires")

The timing of "fire season" in California is variable, depending on the amount of prior winter and spring precipitation, the frequency and severity of weather such as heat waves and wind events, and moisture content in vegetation. [Northern California](/wiki/Northern_California "Northern California") typically sees wildfire activity between late spring and early fall, peaking in the summer with hotter and drier conditions. Occasional cold frontal passages can bring wind and lightning. The timing of fire season in Southern California is similar, peaking between late spring and fall. The severity and duration of peak activity in either part of the state is modulated in part by weather events: downslope/offshore wind events can lead to critical fire weather, while onshore flow and Pacific weather systems can bring conditions that hamper wildfire growth.[[8]](#cite_note-8)[[9]](#cite_note-:02-9)

Apart from the NHL-sanctioned trophies, which teams often recognize by putting up banners in the rafters of their arenas, many teams also claim titles which are not represented by trophies, often also by putting up banners in their rafters. One example is the division title or division championship.[[114]](#cite_note-banners-115) The term unambiguously refers to the team that received the most points in its division at the end of the regular season,[[115]](#cite_note-regular_season_division_title-116) but in some previous seasons, for example, from 1926–27 to 1927–28 and from 1981–82 to 1992–93, when the playoffs where organized along divisions, the term without qualification could also refer to the team which won the corresponding playoff series.[[116]](#cite_note-playoff_division_title-117) The NHL has made clear in the past that it only allows teams to recognize regular season division titles.[[117]](#cite_note-division_titles_nyt-118)
